It differs from its sibling [Piecewise Gaussian Transfer Function Widget](7724-piecewise-gaussian-transfer-function-widget.md) by mapping feature vectors to colors via a single distribution rather than composing multiple piecewise Gaussian functions [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a 'Gaussian widget' that maps input feature vectors (points in the domain) to colors using a single Gaussian distribution defined by a center ($mu$) and a spread parameter ($Sigma$ or $epsilon$). It states that 'only a Gaussian widget was used' and that it maps points according to this distribution. The claim contrasts this with a 'Piecewise Gaussian Transfer Function Widget' which composes multiple piecewise Gaussian functions. Since the evidence confirms the method uses a single distribution (one Gaussian widget) rather than composing multiple functions, and the claim accurately reflects this distinction based on the provided text, the evidence supports the claim.
